DIAGNOSIS: Aponeurotic ptosis (levator dehiscence)

Myasthenia gravis and thyroid eye disease have been excluded. The negative ice pack test and absent antibodies rule out neuromuscular transmission defects. The clinical appearance is consistent with levator aponeurosis disinsertion or stretching.

1. Measurement of margin reflex distance and levator function
2. Assessment of upper eyelid crease position and depth
3. Visual field testing
4. Examination of extraocular movements
5. Phenylephrine eye drop test
